tensions: The system's discipline rules are correct and are being overridden. Two trades broke the 7-day minimum hold last week; those two are the only losers (-$27.79 combined), while every multi-day hold profited. Meanwhile the scheduled prompt's position table drifted 11 days stale — carrying ZEC and W as live holdings after both were closed, missing BTC and AVAX entirely — leaving the automation one unreconciled run from publishing invented numbers. The fee tier also degraded 0.75% to 0.95% taker, making churn 27% more expensive exactly as churn rose. Resolution: edit the stored task's table, and treat the 7-day hold as binding rather than advisory.

opening.text: The book is $1,984.47 against $1,231 deposited — up 61.2%. Realized $400.49 month-to-date on an 11.76% rate. That is the headline and it is a good one. But this scan opened against a position table eleven days dead: it listed ZEC as the largest holding and W beside it, and both were gone — W sold Sep 28, ZEC closed Oct 1. BTC and AVAX had appeared without ever being written down. Reconciling against the broker is not a formality in this system; it is the only thing standing between us and a dashboard full of fiction.

Regime says wait. BTC dominance 58.7%, Fear and Greed 72 and cooling from 74, BTC up 1.54% over seven days against a median alt of 1.51%. That three-hundredths-of-a-point gap is noise, not a signal, so the Step 1b rotation check does not fire however much the dominance number flirts with the 58% line. Thirty-day prints say where we are in the move: NEAR +161%, INJ +59%, AVAX +56%, ONDO +49%, LTC +44%. Buying greed-72 after that run is chasing. The $265.48 stays in cash, and that is a position, not an absence of one.

Here is the part worth paying for. The seven-day minimum hold broke twice last week and both breaches are the only losing trades in the stretch. SUI: bought Sep 25 at 20:22, sold at 22:53 — two and a half hours — minus $6.82. QNT: bought Sep 27 at 23:58, sold Sep 28 at 22:06 — twenty-two hours — minus $20.97. Combined, minus $27.79. Every position given multiple days to work made money. The rule was never a constraint on good trades; it was the thing preventing bad ones, and overriding it produced a perfect two-for-two record of loss.

A quieter leak: Robinhood moved the fee tier the wrong way, 0.75% to 0.95% taker, somewhere between Sep 21 and Sep 25. Roughly $26.10 in explicit fees across twelve days — 1.32% of the book, call it 40% annualized at this trade rate. The v5.7.22 fee model assumes 1.5% per side and still roughly holds once spread is added, so the model is not the problem. The trade frequency is. Weights are clean — LINK 20.8%, XLM 18.4%, nothing near the 25% cap — so nothing in the book forces action. Doing nothing today is the highest-expected-value move available.
